findings.title: canMap* drops realm admin role / manage fallback
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission(client, ...) and never check root.hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_CLIENTS) or manage permission. A caller with the manage-clients realm role or global MANAGE permission therefore loses role-mapping ability under V2, a privilege regression versus V1 and versus canManage/canConfigure in the same file which do check the role. Fix by OR-ing the admin-role / manage check as done for other operations.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission includes All-clients type resource
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and adds resource.getName() for every granted resource. That enumeration includes the 'All clients' placeholder resource named 'Clients' created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init. The returned set will then contain the literal 'Clients' string, which is not a client UUID, polluting list/filter results and lookups. Filter out the type resource or resources whose name equals the type.

findings.title: Removal listener can throw UnsupportedOperationException when V2 enabled
findings.body: registerListener is now guarded only by Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, whose clients().setPermissionsEnabled / roles()/groups() V2 paths throw UnsupportedOperationException. With both features enabled the ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent handler will call the V2 implementation and throw, breaking client/role/group deletion. Guard must exclude V2 (e.g. require V1 enabled and V2 disabled) or dispatch to V1 implementation.

findings.title: getScope NPE on unknown/null resourceType
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes().contains(...) without null-checking the map lookup. An unknown or null resourceType causes NullPointerException (500) instead of ModelValidationException (400). This is reachable from permission creation/update paths with an invalid type. Add explicit null check for the ResourceType before dereferencing.

findings.title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
findings.body: getResourceName only special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE ('All users' / username lookup) and falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. Client resources store the client UUID as name, so admin-permission representations for Clients will show UUID/null instead of clientId/client name. Add a CLIENTS branch mirroring the user branch (all-clients label plus clientId lookup, throwing ModelIllegalStateException if missing).
